title: Obfuscratic Instance Register - sampling frame pre-registration
description: A frame is a rule for enumerating events, fixed and published BEFORE any item in it is coded. The frame is the load-bearing artifact of the register: the directional test is only as defensible as the rule that decided which events could enter it. A frame whose rule could not return counter-directional events is void.

enumerable.description: Whether the full population of items in the window can be listed independently of their content. If false the frame may not be used; salience-selected sources are not frames.

api_or_bulk.description: How the enumeration is obtained reproducibly.

enumeration_rule.description: The exact query or filter that defines the population. Must be mechanically re-runnable by a third party to reproduce the same item list.

population_size.description: Count returned by the enumeration rule. Recorded before coding begins.

coding_target.description: Exhaustive is preferred. Any sampling scheme must be specified here before coding, with its seed.

argument.description: Why this frame's rule can return direction <= -1 items. This is the frame's answer to the selection-on-the-dependent-variable charge and is published with it.

worked_examples.description: At least two concrete item types within this frame that, if they appear, would code negative. Named before coding starts.

expected_direction_share.description: Locked prediction. Stating it before coding is what makes the result capable of embarrassing the analyst.

falsification_trigger.description: The observed result at or beyond which the directional claim for this frame is treated as disconfirmed. Stated as a number, before coding.

status.description: Only 'closed' frames may carry a published statistic. Amendments are dated additions, never silent edits.
